correctness.rationale: For n=2..7 and list bounds L=1,2, exact optimal cardinalities are respectively [1,2,2,2,4,5] and [2,3,4,4,7,11]. A binary incidence matrix records whether received length-(n-2) word is a distinct ordered subsequence of each candidate codeword. Explicit valid primal codebooks reach every claimed optimum. For every candidate column, nonnegative integral dual weights and slacks satisfy incidence weight plus slack >=d, yielding |C|<=floor((L sum weights+sum slacks)/d). Independent checker reconstructs deletion shadows, checks all column inequalities and each listed codebook, including n7 dual d=59 and upper bound floor(666/59)=11. At n7, 11>2*5, while no smaller n has the strict inequality. This is exhaustive finite certification for n<=7, not an asymptotic extrapolation.

value.rationale: Determining the earliest length where a list-two two-deletion code cannot be represented as a union of two uniquely decodable codes is a sharp structural property of synchronization-channel coding.
